pages.title: Cheese Grater
pages.text: Cheese Grater plays in Vancouver, the first of twelve races in Skitchin', EA's 1994 skating game for the Sega Genesis (the Mega Drive outside North America). At about 177 beats a minute, it's the fastest song in the game. The race is 7.2 kilometers long, and its password is TOTEM, after the totem poles in Stanley Park.

pages.title: Made in Vancouver
pages.text: Skitchin' was made in Vancouver, at EA Canada in Burnaby, the studio formerly known as Distinctive Software. Designer Dave Warfield remembers the Stanley Park seawall crowded with inline skaters in 1994.

pages.title: The best city to learn in
pages.text: According to a tip hidden in the game, Vancouver is the best place to learn skitching, because the cars there always keep to the left lane. Skate down the center line and grab one as it goes by.

pages.title: Jeff van Dyck's bedroom studio
pages.text: Composer Jeff van Dyck grew up in Vancouver. His father, a studio musician who also worked as an engineer for Roland, brought home prototype synths and drum machines. By the time Jeff was 13, his father had given him a whole 8-track studio in his bedroom.
